newsitem.title: DENMARK: Novo says Q1 97 likely to be down on Q1 96.
newsitem.headline: Novo says Q1 97 likely to be down on Q1 96.

text.p: Danish pharmaceutical group Novo Nordisk on Wednesday repeated an earlier forecast that 1996 first quarter profits would be lower that the same period the year before but went on to explain why.

"For the first thing, there was a financial income of 50 million crowns in the first quarter of 1996 from hedging of the Japanese yen that Novo Nordisk will not get in 1997," deputy managing director Kurt Anker Nielsen told Reuters.
"For another, sales in the fourth quarter of last year were better than expected and Novo Nordisk cannot exclude the possibility that this was due to a certain amount of advance sales," he added.

A third factor, he said, was that group reorganisation had brought higher costs at the beginning of 1997 than at the start of the year before, but that this would be rectified by the end of the year with a new cost-cutting programme.
The group forecasts full-year 1997 pre-tax profits 15 percent up on 1996's 2.5 billion crowns.
First quarter 1997 results are to be published on May 14. Novo Nordisk posted a 1996 first quarter pre-tax profit of 557 million crowns.

Chairman Vagn Andersen said earlier on Wednesday that the group aimed to be one of the world's most profitable pharmaceutical companies by the turn of the century with a profit margin of at least 20 percent, compared to 16 percent in 1996. --Soeren Linding Jakobsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33 969653
